reuse.why: Several consumers adopt getScheduledAmount, but the API introduces a separate resolver and both resolvers reproduce the existing getApproxNumberThreshold calculation.

duplication.why: The API duplicates schedule amount resolution, and the shared schedule helper duplicates the existing approximate-number tolerance calculation.

placement.why: The shared schedules module is the appropriate home for expected-amount policy, but getExpectedScheduleAmount places another implementation in the API serialization layer.

scope.why: All edits concern schedule amount planning, API exposure, or associated tests.

maintainability.why: Independent policy implementations, retained caller-side dispatch, and an optional untyped operator require maintainers to coordinate future rule changes across multiple locations.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts implements getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of calling shared/schedules.ts:getScheduledAmount; server/schedules/app.ts:updateActions retains missing/numeric dispatch outside that helper.

disguised_duplication.where: server/api-models.ts:getExpectedScheduleAmount reshapes the shared amount resolver through reordered dispatch and different endpoint arithmetic; approximate tolerance arithmetic also repeats shared/rules.ts:getApproxNumberThreshold.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount adds optional op and an isapprox branch; scheduleModel.toExternal uses an independent resolver, while updateActions delegates only ranges and retains the other amount decisions locally.
